title: The Welsh pub named alongside Tower of London as most haunted places in Britain
excerpt: It dates back to at least 1100 and convicts were hanged in its stairwell during its dark medieval past
content:
It dates back to at least 1100 and convicts were hanged in its stairwell during its dark medieval past

03:00, 10 Oct 2026Updated 13:20, 10 Oct 2026

We’re officially in spooky season here in Wales. The air’s crisp, the pumpkins are carved, and the trick or treat sweeties are being purchased. With the big night just around the corner there’s no better time for thrill-seekers and ghost hunters to plan a haunting pub visit or spooky stay, and where better to chase a chill down your spine than in the haunted corners of Wales?

‌

‌

While we have many eerie places here, one pub in particular has a reputation for being one of the haunted places in Wales, the Skirrid Inn, located near Abergavenny. Time Out magazine previously listed places across the world that are most likely to creep you out, and the historic Skirrid Inn was one of them, and one of only three UK sites named in the list, joining landmark paranormal buildings such as the Tower of London and Edinburgh Castle.

‌

It's a well-earned spot on the list as the Skirrid Mountain Inn is said to be one of the oldest and most haunted pubs in Wales. It dates back to at least 1100 and convicts were hanged in its stairwell during its dark medieval past.

‌

It's believed that the inn was used as a rallying point for local supporters of the revolt against Henry IV, led by the rebellious Owain Glyndwr. Legend has it that Welsh icon Glyndwr used the pub’s courtyard to rally his men before raiding settlements sympathetic to the English close by.

The historic inn also features in the Ye Olde Good Inn Guide, a handbook guide to Britain’s most historic watering holes. Its author, James Moore, said the Skirrid Mountain Inn could be one of the oldest surviving pubs in Britain.

‌

He said: “As well as being used as a jolly meeting place, it has a darker history. The pub was used as a jail and as a courtroom, where it is believed 200 convicts were executed by hanging over the stairwell."

Among the ghosts said to be at the Skirrid Inn are the hanging judge, who wanders the upper floors, and the hangman himself. But there are also said to be several friendly ghosts, including local clergyman Father Henry Vaughn, and also a barmaid who died of consumption when working at the inn.

‌

Pub owner Geoff Fiddler told Wales Online that the pub is haunted by several spirits. Geoff explained: “The main ‘resident ghost’ is a lady called Fanny Price who died in the 1800s. Her gravestone is perfectly visible just 300 meters away up the road. Before she’s seen or sensed, there’s a strong smell of lavender perfume – the kind you associate with your grandmother, that sort of musty, lavender smell – and the crinkling of a dress."

There have been numerous ghostly sightings, and Haunted Happenings also hosts popular ghost-hunting events here. They write: "So many ghostly happenings have been reported here that it has earned a reputation for being a terrifying and very intimidating place to spend the night. Most of our guests report that there has been a sinister atmosphere around them, and in some of the rooms they have felt fearful and unwilling to enter them."

The pub has even been previously featured on the popular Most Haunted, with host Yvette Fielding saying it was her favourite place to visit in Wales for ghostly activity. "When we did an investigation, a lot happened. We had alarms going off, shadows moving, doors opening and closing, with tables being violently thrown."

However, despite the pub’s bloody and varied history, Geoff has not had many scary experiences. “It was daytime and it was the sort of figure you see on a Toby jug – a coachman with a tri-cornered hat and almost like a long, scarlet coat on. People always asked if I was scared, and for some reason, I wasn’t. The thought of it scares me, but in that moment, it was more amazement than fright. It was over in a glance, and over the years, I’ve tried to convince myself that I didn’t see it, but I know I did.”
